items.stem: A store owner wants a product sold in three sizes and two colours shown on a single product page with its own stock count per combination. How should this be modelled?

options.text: As one product with size and colour options generating variants, each variant tracking its own inventory
options.rationale: Correct: variants represent purchasable combinations of a single product and each can hold its own stock and price.

options.text: As six separate products linked in a collection
options.rationale: Separate products fragment the page and lose the single-page selector the owner asked for.

options.text: As one product with the sizes listed only in the description text
options.rationale: Free-text sizes are not selectable or trackable as stock.

options.text: As a collection with no products until checkout
options.rationale: A collection groups products; it is not a substitute for a product with variants.

items.explanation: Correct: variants represent purchasable combinations of a single product and each can hold its own stock and price.

items.stem: Which TWO settings directly affect what a customer is charged at checkout, rather than only how the store looks? (Select TWO.)

options.text: The shipping rates configured for the customer's destination
options.rationale: Correct: shipping rates are added to the order total at checkout.

options.text: The tax rules that apply to the product and region
options.rationale: Correct: tax configuration changes the amount the customer pays.
A hero image is presentation and does not change the charge.

options.text: The font chosen in the theme
options.rationale: Typography is cosmetic and has no effect on the total.

items.explanation: Correct: shipping rates are added to the order total at checkout.

items.stem: Before launch, the owner previews the store only on their laptop and it looks correct. Why is that insufficient?

options.text: A large share of shoppers arrive on mobile, so the layout and checkout must be tested at phone width too
options.rationale: Correct: responsive behaviour and mobile checkout must be verified because much traffic is mobile.

options.text: Previews are always wrong and must be ignored
options.rationale: Previews are useful; the gap is only that one screen size was checked.
Laptops render the storefront fine; the issue is untested screen sizes.

options.text: Mobile uses a completely different catalogue
options.rationale: The catalogue is the same; only the presentation adapts.

items.explanation: Correct: responsive behaviour and mobile checkout must be verified because much traffic is mobile.
